subject: S-02
question: who changes "store's country"
reach: cross-cutting: markets and the seller's country
reading: A reading: the store's country is changed where it is held, in the store's general settings (CM-ACC-006: Zid's دولته في إعدادات المتجر under manage.store.settings, WooCommerce's store address under the settings permission, BigCommerce's Default Country under Manage Settings) and, on Shopify, on the business entity behind SELECT_EXISTING_LEGAL_ENTITY and Shopify Support (CM-ACC-004). WooCommerce's "cannot be changed later" (S02-WC-182, S02-WC-230) is WooPayments' account country alone, CM-PAY-002's. The seller, a staff role or the platform's support changing it is each platform's core; the thing changed is the seller's country, which every area reads (S02-E2), so cross-cutting.

subject: S-02
question: what must hold before "store's country" changes
reading: A reading: the conditions on a change of country are those of the record that holds it: Shopify's on the business entity (financial services deactivated, the store and billing addresses in an active entity's country, centralLegalEntitiesEnabled, additional verification: CM-ACC-004, whose cell cites SH-S-0250 and SH-S-0251); Zid's, BigCommerce's and WooCommerce's on the store's settings (a street and district on Zid's save, BigCommerce's "at any time", WooCommerce's save: CM-ACC-006); and Zid's wallet brought to zero first, or settled through customer service, the merchant wallet's own condition (CM-PLN-006). Conditions a capability holds, so capability.

subject: S-02
question: what decides "Shopify Contracting Party"
reach: cross-cutting: markets and the seller's country
reading: A reading: the company a merchant contracts with is CM-ACC-002's thing, where all five answer by their terms: Shopify by the store's billing address, BigCommerce by the merchant's Country of Residence, WooCommerce by residence in the Designated Countries, Zid by the country site (Zid Egypt), Salla with one company for every store. Shopify's "the entity that corresponds to your Designated Country" (S02-SH-030) is the Shopify Payments agreement's party alone, with its Payment Facilitator and Acquirer arrangements, CM-PAY-004's. Every contract names a contracting party, keyed on the seller's country through S02-E2, so cross-cutting.

subject: S-02
question: what decides "Regional Terms"
reach: cross-cutting: markets and the seller's country
reading: A reading: which terms and law govern a merchant is CM-ACC-002's thing (Shopify's Ontario law and billing-address courts, Automattic's California law and EEA, Swiss and UK users, Zid's Saudi law and the laws of the country the service is used from, BigCommerce's table by residence, Salla's one agreement for every user). The payment service's own terms answer in CM-PAY-004: Shopify's Regional Terms by Designated Country with their Payment Facilitator and Acquirer, the Stripe Services Agreement by the Stripe Account Country under WooPayments, Salla's payment services contract signed in verification. Shopify's Managed Markets Terms and self-billing agreement for UK and Canadian stores are CM-MKS-003's. Every contract has its terms, so cross-cutting.

subject: S-02
question: what decides "Business verification documents"
reading: A reading: the documents a business gives are asked on the record of the business, CM-ACC-004 (Shopify's entity form per country and type, with a Yemeni company's government identifiers; Zid's requirements by activity type and country, with the Saudi Business Center for Saudi merchants), and in the payment service's verification, CM-PAY-003 (Salla's store verification per country, Shopify's checks under Germany's regulations and Bizum's tax ID, WooPayments' business types per country). Salla's country chosen at registration decides them (CM-ONB-001, SA-S-0141); Shopify's Managed Markets validates a Canadian or UK tax ID (CM-MKS-003); Zid's sender name asks documents per Gulf country (CM-NTF-004). Checks capabilities run, so capability.

subject: S-02
question: what decides "Shopify Payments"
reading: A reading: what decides whether a store may use the platform's own payment service is CM-PAY-002's thing, where all five answer by the merchant's or store's country (Shopify's Designated Country and an account per business entity, Salla's KNET for Kuwait's stores, Zid Pay for Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, WooPayments' supported countries and registered country, BigCommerce Payments for UK and US stores with a PayPal Business account there). Shopify's card readers, which need the shop country and the location's country to match (S02-SH-588, S02-SH-858), answer in CM-PAY-021; WooCommerce's own Payments settings, which read the stored business location to decide whether WooPayments' onboarding is offered (S02-WC-225 to S02-WC-227, S02-WC-527, S02-WC-528), in CM-PAY-001. A binding behind the market mechanism, so capability.

subject: S-02
question: what decides "Third-party providers"
reading: A reading: which providers other than the platform's own a store may connect is CM-PAY-011's thing, where Shopify (payment options by business location), Zid (Tap for the six Gulf states), BigCommerce (gateway integrations by region, PayPal's and Braintree's supported countries, Fastlane by PayPal) and WooCommerce answer. The store's payment settings that offer them by its country are CM-PAY-001's (WooCommerce's set-up and Business location, BigCommerce's Default country). A flow's own answer lands on its own capability: Shopify's PayPal Express Checkout per business entity (CM-PAY-013), Salla's deferred payment for Kuwait's stores (CM-PAY-015), Salla's bank transfer not available for a country (CM-PAY-030), Shopify's local payment methods for Managed Markets (CM-MKS-003). Capability.
